question: Optimal allocation of an expiring item between two customer classes with different chances of using it before it expires: does the optimal policy depend on the item's remaining lifetime?
expected_direction: No exact match to the consumption-probability formulation, stated openly. Closest: Abouee-Mehrizi 2019, two classes separated by minimum acceptable remaining lifetime, issuing older eligible stock first and possibly reserving fresher stock for high-priority demand - lifetime-dependent through freshness requirements, not through stochastic consumption after allocation. Namekata 1981 uses customer-type arrival probabilities, which are not consumption probabilities. Elicit's own derivation: with immediate allocation and no future opportunity cost, pick the class maximising benefit times P(use before the remaining lifetime elapses); the preferred class changes with lifetime only if that ranking changes.
